correctness.rationale: PASS. For every n>=4, wheel K1∨C_n has KLX=DTC=ceil(n/2)+1, classical stc=3 and tw=3. In any ordered DFS tree with hub root or leaf the hub cut gives n-1 crossing non-tree edges. Otherwise pre-hub ancestors form one nonempty contiguous rim path length a, and all remaining rim vertices belong to hub's unique DFS-child subtree. Its entering and departing tree-edge cuts each cross two rim edges and respectively a or n-a hub spokes, hence backedge crossing-only congestion at least max(a+1,n-a+1). An explicit Hamiltonian DFS path with a=floor(n/2) rim vertices before hub makes all non-tree edges crossing and yields equality; hub star shows stc=3 and width-3 bags with a K4 minor prove tw=3. Boundary n=4 and excluded n=3 noted. Inspected source full traversal/arc verifier; its enumeration of n<=9 and explicit paths to n<=500 are support only, not proof of arbitrary n.

This theorem gives an exact unbounded additive and multiplicative penalty within planar three-connected fixed-treewidth wheel graphs, a structural separation not implied by a general maximum-degree lower bound. The two hub-adjacent cut argument is portable to other apex DFS problems.
